methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ACSL is a publicly listed autonomous systems company on the Tokyo exchange operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation landscape for this stage and sector is constrained: the comp universe comprises six private peers (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air among them) with zero public comparables in the same narrow sector. This composition severely limits traditional triangulation methodologies.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable here. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains five same-sector peers overall, but none satisfy the filtering thresholds required for robust median analysis—specifically, zero companies qualify as same-stage, zero as adjacent-stage, and zero as similar valuation-tier matches. Requiring a minimum of three datapoints per method to ensure statistical validity, a full-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of business models, geographies, and maturity levels across the private peer set.

The absence of public comps and the fragmented nature of the private peer set mean conventional valuation triangulation cannot be reliably applied to ACSL. Any valuation assessment would require either (1) deeper transaction data on the five identified private peers, (2) identification of adjacent-sector public comparables with defensible mapping logic, or (3) fundamental build-up using revenue multiples or DCF assumptions grounded in company-specific financials and market sizing. The current dataset does not support a quantitative valuation range.
